claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions about your circumstances.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to ask you a few more questions about Alex and your situation.

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** For example, is Alex still in school, sixth form, or college studying for A-levels, GCSEs, or similar qualifications?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in school or college at the moment. They've actually started an apprenticeship recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Apprenticeships can count as approved training for Child Benefit purposes.

**Can you tell me more about Alex's apprenticeship? Specifically, is it an approved apprenticeship, and when did it start?** Also, **does Alex work more than 24 hours per week in this apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's an approved apprenticeship here in England. Alex just started it recently. And no, they don't work more than 24 hours a week - it's part-time training.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have a few more questions to complete my assessment.

**How old is Alex exactly - have they turned 17 yet, or are they still 16?** Also, **when exactly did the apprenticeship start?** (I need to know if it was before or after Alex turned 16/17, and whether Alex is still under 20 years old.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is 17 - they've already had their 17th birthday. The apprenticeship started just after they turned 17, so fairly recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you the person responsible for Alex?** In other words, do you live with Alex and are you responsible for their care and upbringing?

Also, **do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives here at home with me. I'm responsible for their care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on my assessment, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why: Child Benefit generally stops when a young person turns 16, unless they are in full-time non-advanced education or approved training. For young people in approved training (like apprenticeships), Child Benefit typically only continues until **31st August following their 16th birthday**.

Since Alex is already 17 and started the apprenticeship after turning 17, they are beyond the age limit for Child Benefit, even though the apprenticeship is approved and Alex works fewer than 24 hours per week.

If Alex's circumstances change - for example, if they were to enter full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels or similar qualifications at a school or college) - you may want to check eligibility again, as Child Benefit can continue until age 20 for young people in qualifying education.

I'm sorry I couldn't give you better news. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
